html:
The Tajik Soviet Socialist Republic became a full republic of the Soviet Union in 1929, with its capital at Dushanbe, until then a village with a Monday market, whose name means Monday.

It had first been drawn in 1924 as part of Uzbekistan, when the Soviets divided Central Asia by nationality. Tajik leaders won full status in 1929 and added the northern district of Khujand, but the great Persian speaking cities of Samarkand and Bukhara stayed in Uzbekistan, a loss still felt.

Dushanbe, renamed Stalinabad from 1929 to 1961, grew into a planned Soviet city with a railway, cotton mills and later aluminium works powered by the Nurek Dam. Writers such as Sadriddin Ayni shaped a Tajik identity in its schools. Independence came in 1991, followed by the civil war.
sum: The Tajik Soviet Socialist Republic became a full republic of the Soviet Union in 1929, with its capital at Dushanbe, until then a village with a Monday market, whose name means Monday.
